READING PASSAGE 2

You should spend about 20 minutes on Questions 14–26, which are based on Reading Passage 2 below.

Playing Soccer

There are many differences between playing soccer in the street and joining a youth team in an organized league in the USA

A Street soccer, as its name implies, is an informal variation of the sport, often played on the street, particularly in urban areas. There are many reasons for the widespread popularity of street soccer. Unlike youth soccer, its more formally organized counterpart, no large space is needed, and goal posts, corner markers, and marked lines, associated with the formal game, are typically absent, as are game officials or referees. Another attraction of street soccer is that it is played frequently and competitively, but does not necessarily require standard 11-a-side teams or fixed playing positions. Unlike in youth soccer, inexperienced street soccer players rarely learn from repetitive technical and tactical drills. Instead, they learn from their poor performance in competition, unconscious of the skills they are nonetheless developing, and without older adults or coaches present. Players learn without effort through playing the game, and soon attain an almost natural feeling for the sport.

B However, there are lots of cities in the world today where conditions are such that street soccer is no longer possible. Congested traffic now dominates where games were once played. Parks and open fields are used as hangouts for older teenagers with other interests. Add to this the requirement in many localities for official permits to use public spaces and the managed schedules that many young people have today, and spontaneous play of any kind is hard to imagine.

C In spite of all these obstacles, which are probably solvable in most instances, there is another sociological explanation of why in many places street soccer doesn't enjoy the same popularity it once did. In his book How Soccer Explains the World, US writer Franklin Foer observes: But for all the talk of freedom, the 1960s parenting style had a far less relaxed side too. Like the 1960s consumer movement which brought seat belts and airbags to cars, the (youth) soccer movement felt like it could create a set of regulations that would protect both the child's body and mind from damage. Soccer leagues like the one I played in as a child handed out ‘participation' prizes to every player, no matter how few games his (or her) team won. Where most of the world accepts the practice of using your head to hit the ball as an essential element of the game, some (youth) soccer parents have worried over the potential for injury to the brain. An entire industry grew up to manufacture protective headgear. Even though very little medical evidence supports this fear, some youth leagues prohibited heading the ball altogether.

D A growing body of people don't believe street soccer involves a legitimate educational method. They argue that children need to be taught by experts. Youth soccer instruction now begins with four-year-olds, so that they will have an advantage as six-year-olds. This need to get ahead brings with it a fear of falling behind that only expert instruction can prevent. This type of instruction leaves no room for the trial-and-error approach of street soccer.

E One of the basic ideas of street soccer is that young players are assigned a particular role by a better player and are expected to play for the good of the team. Such an assignment runs counter to the idea of youth soccer that every child needs to learn every position and will benefit from doing so. In street soccer, you fill the role that you are best able to at a particular time. While this role assignment can change from game to game, the purpose is always the same: to get the best out of each individual at any given moment.

F In street soccer, children have to learn patience, to wait their turn, to realize that they are not entitled to make decisions, or even be listened to simply because they show up. Positions of responsibility are earned through competition within the team. Younger players in street soccer must wait to attain those positions. In youth soccer, however, with its overly democratic values, youngsters are guaranteed their time in the spotlight. Whether it's their turn to be captain, to play a central position or to take a crucial shot, youth soccer players come to believe that hard work and patience aren't really necessary.

G Not only does every youth soccer player get a chance, it is assumed that each individual has played well. ‘Everyone's a winner; no one's a loser' is a guiding principle of youth soccer. This ensures each individual goes away positive about themselves. No one can leave a game or a practice feeling bad. But, if there really are no losers, then why try at all? Since giving less than your best receives the same reward as giving your best, why go to any extra effort? In street soccer, every game results in a winner and a loser and everyone knows who is who. Losing a game is a common experience and players learn early on how to handle this. As a result, unlike most youth soccer players, they acquire resilience. A further difference between these two strands of soccer is that in street soccer a formal record is not kept. You can lose one day and win the next. The results are only temporary and are forgotten within minutes of the end of the match. But in organized youth soccer, the position each person plays and the results are formally noted and maintained throughout a season.

Questions 14–19

Reading Passage 2 has seven sections, A–G.

Which section contains the following information?

Write the correct letter, A–G, to boxes 14–19 on your answer sheet.

ABCDEFG
14 a contrast between the ways young players gain experience of playing different positions
15 examples outside sport of greater emphasis on individual safety
16 a description of methods of selection for leadership on soccer teams
17 details of urban changes that discourage street soccer
18 a mention of the lesson that failure teaches street soccer players
19 an explanation of why youth soccer emphasises the need for coaches

Questions 20 and 21

Choose TWO letters, A–E.

The list below gives some possible reasons for the popularity of street soccer. Which TWO of these reasons are mentioned by the writer of the text?

Questions 22 and 23

Choose TWO letters, A–E.

The list below gives some possible results of the 1960s parenting style. Which TWO of these results are mentioned by Franklin Foer in the excerpt from How Soccer Explains the World?

Questions 24–26

Complete the summary below.

Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer.

Winners and losers

For youth soccer players, a key 24 is that they should always come away from the game with a positive attitude. In this respect, regardless of the effort the players make, they get some kind of 25 at the end of a game. In street soccer, however, players gain resilience because they have to learn to cope with failure. But the outcome of a match isn't remembered for long. In fact, no-one ever keeps a 26 of the results of games.

passageNotes.label: Paragraph A
passageNotes.text: 街头足球是足球的非正式形式，常见于城市街道，普及原因众多：无需大场地，无正式比赛所需的球门柱、角旗、标线及裁判；无需 11 人制球队和固定位置；新手无需重复技术战术训练，通过比赛中的失误自然学习（无成人或教练指导），在玩乐中轻松掌握足球直觉。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph B
passageNotes.text: 如今许多城市已难以开展街头足球：交通拥堵占据原游戏场地，公园成为青少年聚集地，多地需许可才能使用公共空间，且年轻人日程繁忙，自发游戏几乎消失。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph C
passageNotes.text: 除环境障碍外，社会学角度也能解释街头足球 popularity 下降：美国作家富兰克林・福尔（Franklin Foer）在《足球如何解释世界》中指出，20 世纪 60 年代育儿理念既追求自由也注重保护 —— 如同消费者运动推动汽车配备安全带和安全气囊，青少年足球运动试图通过规则保护儿童身心，例如联赛给所有球员发 “参与奖”，部分家长担忧头球伤脑（尽管无医学证据），催生防护装备产业，部分联赛甚至禁止头球。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph D
passageNotes.text: 越来越多人认为街头足球的教育方式不正规，主张儿童需专家指导 —— 青少年足球从 4 岁开始培训，家长担心落后，这种指导排斥街头足球的试错模式。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph E
passageNotes.text: 街头足球中，优秀球员为新手分配特定角色，强调团队利益；而青少年足球主张 “每个孩子需学习所有位置”，两者理念相反。街头足球的角色随比赛变化，核心是 “发挥个人当下最大优势”。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph F
passageNotes.text: 街头足球中，儿童需学会耐心等待、接受无决策权的现实，责任职位需通过队内竞争获得，年轻球员需等待机会；而青少年足球强调 “过度民主”，保证每个孩子有表现机会（如轮流当队长、踢核心位置），使孩子误以为无需努力和耐心。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph G
passageNotes.text: 青少年足球的原则是 “人人获胜，无人失败”，确保孩子积极离场，但这削弱了努力的动力；街头足球有明确胜负，球员早早学会应对失败，培养心理韧性。此外，街头足球无正式记录，胜负转瞬即忘；青少年足球则记录球员位置和赛季成绩。

questionExplanations.sectionTitle: 1. 段落匹配（Questions 14–19：Which section contains the following information?）

items.text:
（1）题目 14：a contrast between the ways young players gain experience of playing different positions（对比年轻球员体验不同位置的方式）
答案：E
解析：定位 Paragraph E 中 “One of the basic ideas of street soccer is that young players are assigned a particular role... Such an assignment runs counter to the idea of youth soccer that every child needs to learn every position”，对比街头足球 “分配特定角色” 与青少年足球 “学习所有位置”，与题干对应，因此答案为 E。

（2）题目 15：examples outside sport of greater emphasis on individual safety（体育外重视个人安全的例子）
答案：C
解析：定位 Paragraph C 中 “Like the 1960s consumer movement which brought seat belts and airbags to cars, the (youth) soccer movement felt like it could create a set of … regulations that would protect both the child’s body and mind from damage”，以 “汽车安全带、安全气囊” 为例，与题干对应，因此答案为 C。

（3）题目 16：a description of methods of selection for leadership on soccer teams（描述足球队 leadership 选拔方式）
答案：F
解析：定位 Paragraph F 中 “Positions of responsibility are earned through competition within the team. Younger players in street soccer must wait to attain those positions... youth soccer players come to believe that hard work and patience aren’t really necessary”，描述街头足球 “竞争 + 等待” 与青少年足球 “无差别分配” 的选拔差异，与题干对应，因此答案为 F。

（4）题目 17：details of urban changes that discourage street soccer（阻碍街头足球的城市变化细节）
答案：B
解析：定位 Paragraph B 中 “Congested traffic now dominates... Parks and open fields are used as hangouts... requirement... for official permits... managed schedules”，列举交通、场地用途、许可制度等城市变化，与题干对应，因此答案为 B。

（5）题目 18：a mention of the lesson that failure teaches street soccer players（提及失败给街头足球球员带来的教训）
答案：G
解析：定位 Paragraph G 中 “Losing a game is a common experience and players learn early on how to handle this. As a result, unlike most youth soccer players, they acquire resilience”，明确提到失败教会球员 “应对能力和韧性”，与题干对应，因此答案为 G。

（6）题目 19：an explanation of why youth soccer emphasises the need for coaches（解释青少年足球强调教练必要性的原因）
答案：D
解析：定位 Paragraph D 中 “They argue that children need to be taught by experts... This need to get ahead brings with it a fear of falling behind that only expert instruction can prevent”，解释 “担心落后，需专家指导”，与题干对应，因此答案为 D。

题目：Which TWO of these reasons are mentioned by the writer of the text?（作者提及的街头足球受欢迎的两个原因）
答案：C、E
选项 C：You do not need elaborate facilities to play street soccer.（无需复杂设施即可玩街头足球）
解析：定位 Paragraph A 中 “no large space is needed, and goal posts, corner markers, and marked lines... are typically absent”，明确提到无需复杂设施，C 正确。
- 选项 E：Street soccer teams can have varying numbers of players.（街头足球队人数灵活）
解析：定位 Paragraph A 中 “does not necessarily require standard 11-a-side teams”，明确提到无需固定 11 人制，人数灵活，E 正确。
- 排除 A：文中无 “著名球员从街头足球起步” 的表述；排除 B：文中未提及 “街头足球适合低龄儿童”；排除 D：文中无 “新手不被批评” 的表述。

题目：Which TWO of these results are mentioned by Franklin Foer?（富兰克林・福尔提及的 20 世纪 60 年代育儿风格的两个结果）
答案：B、D
选项 B：Some youth soccer leagues adopted more restrictive rules of play.（部分青少年足球联赛采用更严格的比赛规则）
解析：定位 Paragraph C 中 “some youth leagues prohibited heading the ball altogether”，明确提到禁止头球等严格规则，B 正确。
- 选项 D：Youth soccer players were sometimes rewarded for simply playing in games.（青少年足球球员有时仅因参赛获奖励）
解析：定位 Paragraph C 中 “Soccer leagues... handed out ‘participation’ prizes to every player, no matter how few games his (or her) team won”，明确提到 “参与奖”，D 正确。
- 排除 A：文中无 “青少年足球成本上升” 的表述；排除 C：文中未提及 “参与人数减少”；排除 E：文中无 “厂商针对家长广告” 的表述。

items.text:
（1）题目 24：For youth soccer players, a key \___\___ is that they should always come away from the game with a positive attitude.
题目翻译：对青少年足球球员而言，核心_\___\__是他们离场时应始终保持积极态度。
答案：principle（原则）
解析：定位 Paragraph G 中 “‘Everyone’s a winner; no one’s a loser’ is a guiding principle of youth soccer. This ensures each individual goes away positive about themselves”，明确提到 “原则”，因此答案为 “principle”。

（2）题目 25：In this respect, regardless of the effort the players make, they get some kind of \___\___ at the end of a game.
题目翻译：因此，无论球员付出多少努力，赛后都会获得某种_\___\__。
答案：reward（奖励）
解析：定位 Paragraph G 中 “giving less than your best receives the same reward as giving your best”，明确提到 “奖励”，因此答案为 “reward”。

（3）题目 26：In fact, no-one ever keeps a \___\___ of the results of games.
题目翻译：事实上，无人记录比赛结果的_\___\__。
答案：record（记录）
解析：定位 Paragraph G 中 “in street soccer a formal record is not kept”，明确提到 “记录”，因此答案为 “record”。
